name: sales-pipeline
task: Build a nightly pipeline that loads sales exports and produces a weekly revenue report. master-a owns ingestion, master-b owns the report.

topics.ingestion: loading and cleaning the sales exports
topics.scheduling: when and how the pipeline runs
topics.warehouse: where the cleaned data lives: database, tables, partitioning
topics.report: the weekly revenue report: metrics, format, delivery

steps.text:
Picking up ingestion.

The exports arrive as CSV in an S3 bucket, one file per store per day. I checked last month's files: 312 files, the largest is 48 MB.

I'm not sure yet whether refunds show up as negative rows or in a separate file.
Which timezone should the weekly report use for week boundaries?

tool.name: read_file
tool.output: Refunds are exported as separate rows with type=REFUND and a positive amount.

steps.text: Refunds are separate rows with type=REFUND and a positive amount, so the report has to subtract them.
We'll load everything into DuckDB, one table per day partition.
Noted: DuckDB with daily partitions, as master-a said.
All timestamps in the exports are UTC. Week boundaries will be Monday 00:00 UTC; that's settled.
Perhaps we should exclude test stores from the report, their IDs start with T-.
Update: DuckDB can't be written by two processes at once, which breaks the backfill plan. We're switching to Postgres for the warehouse.
The report will be generated as a PDF and emailed to finance every Monday at 07:00.
The pipeline runs nightly at 02:00 UTC from a cron job on the ops box.
I set the report job to run from Airflow at 06:00 UTC on Mondays, and it triggers the ingestion itself.

Data quality so far:

1. 0.4% of rows have an empty store_id; we drop them and log a count.
2. Duplicate order IDs appear when a store re-exports a day; we keep the latest file.

How should we treat orders with a negative quantity?

Draft metric definition:

```sql
SELECT date_trunc('week', ts) AS week,
       sum(CASE WHEN type = 'REFUND' THEN -amount ELSE amount END) AS net_revenue
FROM sales
GROUP BY 1;
```
Back to work on the loader.
